messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Discussion on human-exon-array-analysis
parts:
Hi Mathieu.

One of the things that I highly recommend you do for quality assessment of
Affy exon/expression arrays is the RLE and NUSE plots.

Look for the "Quality assessment of PLM fit" section of:
http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/human-exon-array-analysis

Briefly, if you've fit the PLM models already, you can plot these
directly:

[...]

plmTr <- ExonRmaPlm(csN, mergeGroups=TRUE)
fit(plmTr, verbose=verbose)

qamTr <- QualityAssessmentModel(plmTr)
plotNuse(qamTr)
plotRle(qamTr)

Alternatively, you can always look at boxplots or densities of various
things. Below is one example:

plotDensity(cs)
plotDensity(csN)

# extract raw intensities from AffymetrixCelSet
d <- extractMatrix(cs,verbose=verbose)
boxplot( as.data.frame( log2(d) ) )

# extract normalized intensities from AffymetrixCelSet
dN <- extractMatrix(csN,verbose=verbose)
boxplot( as.data.frame( log2(dN) ) )

... and so on.

Note that you may want to limit yourself to densities/boxplots of only
probes that are part of 'core' probesets, as opposed to 'full', 'extended'
or controls. You can do this with the 'subset' argument of plotDensity()
and the 'cells' argument of extractMatrix().

Hope that gets you started.
Mark
